reason: I'll start with the loose cloud to see how the young stars affect it.
expectation: The stars' radiation may heat or disperse the loose gas, though I'm unsure of the outcome.

alternatives.reason: The dense cloud is also a goal, but I want to see the loose cloud's response first.

effect: The loose gas is swept out of the nursery, completing that goal; I'll now follow the dense cloud.
reaction: The contrast between gas becoming stars and being driven away is interesting.
reason: This is the only available combination and addresses what survives the new stars.
expectation: The dense cloud may resist the stars' radiation and outflows better than the loose cloud, though its fate is uncertain.

effect: The dense cloud forms temporary pillars as its exposed surface erodes and its interior shields material, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The contrast with the dispersed loose cloud was satisfying, especially the qualification that the pillars are temporary.

mostWorthwhile.text: The dense-cloud combination made the contrast between erosion and shielding clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second decision was less engaging because only one combination remained, though its result was informative.

surprise.text: The dense cloud survives as temporary pillars rather than remaining untouched.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; each addressed a stated goal.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow the expelled gas and see what happens to the temporary pillars.
